questions.stem: Calculate net filtration pressure with the following data: PGC: 42 mmHgπGC: 12 mmHg; PBC: 16 mmHgAssume that no proteins were filtered.
questions.solutionHtml:
14
  • To calculate the net filtration pressure (NFP), we use the formula:
    • NFP = (PGC - πGC) - PBC
  • where:
    • PGC = Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure
    • πGC = Glomerular capillary osmotic pressure (colloid osmotic pressure)
    • PBC = Bowman's capsule hydrostatic pressure

  • Given the data:
    • PGC = 42 mmHg
    • πGC = 12 mmHg
    • PBC = 16 mmHg
  • Now, let's plug in the values:
    • NFP = (42 - 12) - 16
    • NFP = 30 - 16
    • NFP = 14 mmHg
    • The net filtration pressure is 14 mmHg. 
  • So, the correct answer is:
  • C. 14


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 8 and 9. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no: 337

questions.stem: Which hormones is/are under inhibitory control of hypothalamus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Both GH and prolactin

Both Growth Hormone (GH) and Prolactin are under inhibitory control of the hypothalamus.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 917.

questions.stem: Which hormone has permissive role in puberty?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leptin

Leptin is a hormone produced by adipose (fat) cells and is involved in regulating energy balance and body weight. It plays a permissive role in puberty by signaling the hypothalamus about the body's energy stores.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 391.

questions.stem: The earliest stage at which erythropoietin is effective in red blood cell formation is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Burst forming units
  • Erythropoietin (EPO) is a hormone produced by the kidneys in response to low oxygen levels in the blood. It plays a crucial role in red blood cell formation, also known as erythropoiesis.
  • The earliest stage at which erythropoietin is effective in red blood cell formation is at the "Burst forming unit" (BFU-E) stage.


Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology 13th Edition Page no 428

questions.stem: Which of the following heart sound may be a normal finding during pregnancy?
questions.solutionHtml:
S3
  • An increased S3 may be heard during late pregnancy. This heart sound is heard in early diastole.
  • During pregnancy, it is common for some changes to occur in the cardiovascular system due to the increased demands on the circulatory system. One of the normal findings during pregnancy is the presence of an S3 heart sound.


Williams Obstetrics 25th Edition Page no 61.DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9th edition, Page no: 48

questions.stemHtml: Which cell organelle is absent in cardiac muscle in the region marked by an arrow in the image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lysosome
  • The single nucleus of the cardiac muscle cell is located in the center of the cell. Myofibrils pass around the nucleus, producing a Bi conical juxta nuclear region in which the other organelles are concentrated.
  • This perinuclear region is rich in mitochondria and contains a Golgi apparatus, glycogen granules, and lipofuscin granules. The marking areas are centrally placed nuclei.
  • Note: In a mammalian cell, lysosomes are located near perinuclear region known as “perinuclear cloud.” In cardiac muscle, they are very less in number (not completely absent).


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page nos 37 and 38.

questions.stem: Most effective parameter to decrease blood flow to tissue bed:
questions.solutionHtml:
Diameter of vessel
  • The most effective parameter to decrease blood flow to a tissue bed is the diameter of the blood vessel that supplies the tissue. This is known as vasoconstriction.
  • When the diameter of the blood vessel decreases, it restricts the flow of blood through that vessel, reducing the amount of blood delivered to the tissue bed.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no: 179

questions.stemHtml: Compliance curve of the lung is given below. What does Curve A signify?
questions.solutionHtml:
Emphysema

Curve “A” has higher TLC and higher compliance than normal curve, which is typical of emphysema.

Bronchitis may have high TLC (obstructive disease) but compliance generally remains normal or slightly higher than normal.

  • This is a compliance curve.
  • Left and up in the graph (A): Indicates increased compliance.
  • Right and down in the graph (B): Indicates reduced compliance.
  • Hence the answer is emphysema (increased compliance).
  • All the other disorders mentioned have reduced compliance.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 622.
